glossEn: Are you coming to practice tomorrow?
Call me when you are free.
What are you doing on the weekend?

notes: Marker: T-pronoun ты; the casual greeting привет agrees with it.

text: Вы не могли бы мне помочь?
notes: Marker: V-pronoun вы with plural agreement могли бы; V-form maps to polite.

text: Садитесь, пожалуйста, доктор вас сейчас примет.
glossEn: Please have a seat, the doctor will see you shortly.
notes: Marker: V-imperative садитесь and V-accusative вас addressed to one person (a patient).

text: Здравствуйте, Анна Петровна! Как вы себя чувствуете?
glossEn: Hello, Anna Petrovna! How are you feeling?
notes: Marker: name-plus-patronymic address (Анна Петровна) with V-pronoun вы and V-greeting здравствуйте.

glossEn: Could you tell me the time, please?
notes: Marker: V-imperative скажите (the T-form would be скажи).

glossEn: Are you getting off at the next stop?
notes: Marker: V-pronoun вы with выходите, the standard polite question to a stranger.

text: Спасибо большое! Ты меня очень выручил.
glossEn: Thanks a lot! You really helped me out.
notes: Trap: спасибо is a fossilized formula and sets no register; the T-pronoun ты with 2sg выручил fixes the sentence as casual.

glossEn: Please pass on to him: 'call me tomorrow.'
notes: Trap: the quoted T-imperative позвони is casual, but the frame's V-imperative передайте addresses the hearer politely; the frame's register governs.

text: Поезд в Москву отправляется в восемь часов.
glossEn: The train to Moscow departs at eight.
notes: Third-person statement with no addressee and no T/V form.

glossEn: In winter it is very cold in Siberia.
The museum is closed on Mondays.
